tagline.text: A hidden beach on Matinloc Island that you reach by swimming through a gap in the rock

location.label: Location
location.text: West side of Matinloc Island, Bacuit Bay, El Nido, Palawan

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: November–May dry season (tours may be cancelled during the November–January northeast winds)

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: About 1 hour within a Tour C day

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,800–2,500 (Tour C shared fare, environmental fee and Matinloc entrance fee combined)

children.text: Secret Beach is a small white-sand beach hidden behind limestone cliffs on the west side of Matinloc Island, reached only by swimming through a narrow gap in the rock wall. It is a stop on Tour C, where you spend roughly one hour of the day, and when the sea is rough the boats sometimes skip it.

Secret Beach is a small beach on the west side of Matinloc Island in Bacuit Bay, off El Nido. High limestone cliffs enclose it, so the beach cannot be seen from the sea and boats cannot enter. You anchor the bangka outside and swim through a narrow gap in the rock wall, and this adventure-like approach is the beach's charm. One guide lists the trip from El Nido town at about
2 hours
by bangka, but it varies with the tour schedule and weather.

The only public way to get there is practically El Nido's island-hopping Tour C, although you can also charter a private bangka. Besides Secret Beach, Tour C includes Matinloc Shrine, Hidden Beach, Helicopter Island and snorkeling near Star Beach, and lunch is often included. Tours are listed as leaving town between 8:30 and 9:00 and returning around 4:30 PM, so confirm the exact schedule with your operator.
One guide describes the inside as a crescent of sand about

long, while others mention only a few meters of sand, but all agree the space is tiny. Limestone walls tens of meters high rise around it like a folding screen, and the water shifts from turquoise to deep green. Sources say there are no toilets, vendors or shade, so bring water, snacks and a dry bag or leave them on the boat.

A local legend says this place inspired Alex Garland's novel The Beach, but that is not a confirmed fact. Several accounts say that on days of rough sea or swell, especially during the northeast winds of November–January, many boats skip Secret Beach and go somewhere else instead. Ask your tour operator the day before whether Secret Beach is open.

blocks.title: Swimming In Through a Gap in the Rock

children.text: You get off the bangka, swim about

to a narrow gap in the cliff, and pass through when the waves pull back. One source describes the gap as barely wider than a person. Reviews say the water becomes shallow inside the gap and a large rock can knock swimmers around, so follow your guide's signals.

blocks.title: A Secret Beach Walled in by Cliffs

children.text: Past the gap, a cozy white beach hemmed in by tall limestone walls appears. Accounts say the view looks best in the morning, when sunlight falls between the walls. Because the beach is small, it is a place to rest briefly and enjoy the scenery rather than stay long.
In the shallow water near the gap you can see coral and small tropical fish. One guide lists visibility at about
. Snorkeling gear is often included in the tour, but confirm when you book.

blocks.title: An Entrance That Changes with the Tide

children.text: At low tide you can reportedly walk or wade through without going under, but at high tide you must duck your head briefly under the rock and the beach gets smaller. Another source says the calmest conditions are best and the boatman decides when it is safe to go in.

Tour C also stops at Matinloc Shrine and Hidden Beach. One account says the shrine was built in 1982 and construction stalled over permit problems, and Hidden Beach is a secluded beach on the east side of Matinloc Island. Both involve swimming in water ringed by limestone.

blocks.title: Snorkeling at Helicopter Island and Star Beach

children.text: Around lunchtime you snorkel in the sea near Helicopter Island and Star Beach. Parrotfish, Moorish idols, nudibranchs and moray eels are mentioned. One account says Star Beach itself is private, so you cannot enter the beach.

blocks.title: An Island Boat Ride from Town

children.text: The trip from El Nido town to Secret Beach is a boat ride out through the limestone islands of Bacuit Bay. Emerald water and sheer cliffs line the way, so the tour itself is a sight to see.
Gather at the El Nido town pier. The check-in place can differ by operator, so check your booking confirmation.
Set off by bangka. On a private tour, leaving an hour early so you reach Secret Beach first before the crowds is a suggested approach.
Arrive at Secret Beach, anchor the bangka and swim through the gap in the rock. Tour C usually arrives between about 9 and 11 AM, when the light is good.
At Matinloc Shrine, listen to the guide's account of the site's history and climb to the viewpoint.
Have lunch at Hidden Beach or near Star Beach. Lunch is usually described as a buffet with seafood and fruit.
Snorkel in the sea near Helicopter Island and Star Beach.
Return to the town pier. One listing gives the return time as about 4:30 PM.
The exact order of stops and times vary with the operator and weather. Tour C is the longest and roughest of the tours, so consider a different tour if you are a weak swimmer.
Leave town on the private bangka you reserved the day before.
Reach Secret Beach first and go in when the water is calm.
Leave before the tour boats crowd in and move on to Matinloc Shrine and Hidden Beach.
Have lunch and snorkel near Star Beach.
Return to town.

2026 guides list small local charters from about ₱6,000, an outrigger for two at about ₱13,000–14,000, and one operator from ₱16,000, so prices differ widely by boat type and operator. Confirm the exact price with the operator.
In some seasons there are direct flights from Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) in Manila to El Nido Airport (ENI). Check airline notices for operation and schedules.
You can also fly into Puerto Princesa International Airport (PPS) and continue overland by van. Check travel time and fares locally.
Direct flights to El Nido Airport have strict baggage weight limits, so pack light.

items.title: From El Nido Town to Secret Beach

children.text: One guide says it takes about
2 hours
by bangka from El Nido town to Secret Beach. It is included in Tour C, and sources say there is no separate entrance fee.
If you charter a private bangka, ask the operator to include Secret Beach on the route.
The boat stays outside, and you swim about
in wearing a life jacket.
You can book Tour C at travel agencies in El Nido town or on online booking sites. Advice is to book at least a day ahead, and earlier in peak season.
Tour prices in town are said to be fixed, so switching operators changes the price little, but check what is included.
Some guides say you need to bring your ID when booking.

Secret Beach is easiest to enter on days when the sea is calm. The dry season from November to May is generally stable, but during the northeast winds (Amihan) of November–January the waves can rise and many boats skip Secret Beach. March–May usually brings clear skies and relatively calm seas.

Mornings are better. Tour C usually arrives at about 9–11 AM when the light is good, and sources say afternoons get hot with no shade. In peak season from December to May and on holidays, crowds can fill the beach, so going early on a private tour is a suggested approach.

In the rainy season from June to October, tours are often cancelled because of rain and rough seas. Tour C goes farthest, so it is said to be the most affected by weather. If an operator cancels for weather, it reportedly offers a new date or a refund.

Secret Beach trips mostly start from El Nido town. The town has lodging from guesthouses and hostels to beach resorts, and a place near the pier makes an early start easier. Book early in peak season.

Lunch on Tour C is a buffet on an island beach, described as meats, crustaceans, seafood, fruit and vegetables. You may bring extra food and drinks, but trash must go only in the designated bins. There is no vendor inside Secret Beach, so bring plenty of water. Back in town, the restaurant strip offers seafood.
Ask your tour operator the day before whether Secret Beach is open.
Wear water shoes, and keep your phone and camera in a dry bag or waterproof case.
If you are a weak swimmer, wear a life jacket and tell the boatman beforehand.
At the gap, wait for the waves to pull back and do not rush through.
Going early in the morning means fewer people and better light.
Keep your environmental fee receipt and show it for each tour.
The Matinloc Shrine fee is often paid in cash on site, so have small bills ready.
Drones are restricted by local rules, so check before you bring one.
The gap into Secret Beach can be dangerous even for experienced swimmers when the sea is rough. If the sea is rough, do not go in and follow the boatman's judgment.
A large rock sits just inside the gap, and waves can push you into it and hurt your knees or body. Wear shoes and move slowly.
At high tide you must duck your head under the rock, so protect your eyes and nose.
There are no toilets, vendors or shade on the beach, so it is hard to stay long. Midday is very hot.
In November–January and the rainy season, tours are often cancelled or skip Secret Beach, so leave slack in your schedule.
Do not step on or touch coral and marine life, and take your trash with you.
The town where the tours to Secret Beach depart, with lodging, restaurants and tour operators.

children.text: Lagoons visited on El Nido Tour A, different from Secret Beach. It is best to go on a separate day from Tour C.
Visited with Secret Beach on Tour C, with a building begun in 1982 whose construction stalled and a viewpoint.

5 minutes
